claim: Two units disagree on what land a camp may take. V01 §3.16 calls `campLand` "the outskirts' land a camp look may take" (l.2360–2371). It is never wood, marsh, quarry, garden or orchard, and lies within `camp.reachM`. V01 §1b's wiring row (l.283) names `beyondWalls` among its readers, and R2-37 (5) rules "The outskirts' land is V01's `campLand` … §10.2's placement rules rank them". But §10.2 *Crisis looks* (d)'s `beyondWalls` (l.15376–15378) takes "the land faces at least `siegeStandoffM` beyond … (`campLand`'s **and the hinterland's land-use faces** there)": any wood, orchard, quarry, marsh or crop field, at any distance. `approachRoads` (l.15379) defines a second, unbounded set of "verges of each arterial" beside `campLand` (2)'s. (e)'s cap, "`densityCap` of the outskirts' free land" (l.15399), then has no single denominator. So the siege camps stand on land V01 says no camp takes, and the cap's base differs with the reader.
required_change: §10.2 *Crisis looks* (d): "`beyondWalls` — the `campLand` faces (V01 §3.16) lying at least `siegeStandoffM` beyond the outermost standing enceinte's outer strip along its walled arcs; a closure arc with no wall draws none"; "`approachRoads` — `campLand`'s verges of each arterial leaving the settlement (V01 §3.16 (2)), one camp per road; a road with none, and a place no road reaches (…), take the `campLand` nearest its boundary"; (e): "together at most `densityCap` of `campLand`'s free land". (f)'s trenches, earthworks and burned farmsteads, which are no camp, keep their own places. V01 §1b's `campLand` row then reads "`approachRoads`" for "`approachRoads`' fallback" (V01's end, R2-05).

V07 §1 (15) (l. 197–200) hands §10.2 'its places read at the village rungs as V07 §5.6 (2) states'. §10.2 *Crisis looks*, the placement home, does not carry that end: (d) defines the main approach road by §4.3's `TradeFlow` and `affectedQuarter` as 'the district …', and only `neighbourhoods` cites V07; (f) draws `siege`'s 'line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs' at every rung with walled arcs, which §8.2's siege row (l. 12892) draws. V07 §5.6 (1) (l. 3400–3402) and T-V7-69 draw no siege line at THORP or HAMLET — item 122 (c)'s 'a hamlet gets a war band's camp, a city a full siege line', which §13.2's T122-5 (l. 18159) also quotes — and no V11 `scale` cell can suppress the line (they are camped-ground areas). The base and V07 draw a hamlet's siege differently.
required_change: ONE FIX with VV78-r2-05, in its words: §10.2 (c) adds that a share s of a place's n units takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s > 0 and none where s ≤ 0 (V01 §3.16 (5)'s count); (d) adds 'at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the main approach road, the outskirts' land and each place below read on the village's records as V07 §5.6 (2) states, `affectedQuarter` a unit of V07 §5.6 (3)'; (f)'s `siege` reads 'at VILLAGE and above, a line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs at it — none at THORP and HAMLET, item 122 (c)'s war band's camp (V07 §5.6 (1))'; (h) adds 'and no siege line at THORP and HAMLET'. §8.2's siege row draws the line where §10.2 places it and needs no change.

claim: The dossier cadence has three triggers in its producer and two in its home. V08 §3.6 (3) (l.1826-1840) folds an epoch at each year end, at each ± 5 % population crossing, 'and an epoch at the week of each newly carried calamity that no other epoch falls on (a destructive event is epoch content, §4.11's rung at an epoch)'. J-V8.55 (V08 l.3416) records this as citing '§4.11's cadence — … plus one at each new calamity's week'. §4.11 *The clock* (4) (l.8293-8299), the cadence's home, states only a 52-week boundary or a population move past the roster tolerance ('No epoch is folded per tick'). V06 §3.3.1 restates those two triggers (VAT2-r2-02), and `EpochInputs.events[].week` 'in (the previous epoch's week, week]' (l.8184) reads a calamity as riding the epoch whose span holds it. A port built from the home therefore folds a calamity of week 10 into the next year-end epoch, and while the dossier's present lies before that year end the calamity is not in the model at all. A port built from V08 folds it in its own week. Every reader of that epoch is affected: V06 §3.22 (1)'s aftermath, V06 §3.13 (2)'s hazard week, V04's burial deaths, and V01 §3.16 (2)'s disaster calamity read from 'the committed `epoch` events' (V01 l.2327-2330, l.343). At the present week of a fresh calamity no committed event holds it, so the look strikes the scatter pattern with no matched target, against item 122 (b)'s 'the calamity's `targets` win', and changes its units when the epoch later folds. The agreement matrix has no cadence row.
required_change: §4.11 *The clock* (4): after 'by more than the **roster tolerance**, ± 5 % (J-A76.43; the one number §7.7 item 3's lapse reads too)' insert '— and at the week of each newly carried calamity that no other epoch falls on (DR28: a destructive event is epoch content; V08 §3.6 (3); J-V8.55)'. Keep the catch-up clause 'coarsened under item 119's comfort level by V06 §6.8 (6)'; a coarse catch-up carries a calamity in the coarse epoch that holds its week. V06 §3.3.1 states the same three triggers in the same round (VAT2-r2-02; R2-05).

claim: 'The creation week' has two meanings, and the first epoch's span reads it. (1) The present: §4.11 *The clock* (1) (l.8275-8276) says 'Its creation week is the present week of the dossier it is created from; a standalone map starts at week 0'. V06 §3.20.3 (l.3117) takes `W_p` as 'the present — the document's creation week (§4.11 *The clock* (1))', and V06 l.409 and EP-15 (l.8801, 'a replay starting 300 years before a week-0 creation') use the same meaning. (2) The first model's week: a history-first document's `generate` event stands at `W_p − round(52 × start.yearsAgo)` (V06 §3.20.3). V06 §2.11's `HistoryIndex.creationWeek` (l.809) is 'the week of the log's first model: a replayed document's first replay epoch's start', and V06 §3.15.2's `locate` (l.2317-2319) and §3.15.4's bar (l.2352) read that meaning. The span: `EpochInputs.years` is '(week − the previous epoch's week, or the creation week) ÷ 52' (l.8182), and V06's `ProductEpochContext.prevWeek` (l.467) and V06 §3.1 (3) (l.953-955) say the same. Under the home's definition the first replay epoch's `years` is (W_p − 52·toYearsAgo₁ − W_p) ÷ 52, which is below 0. Every per-year chance `1 − (1 − p)^years` (§4.11 *The clock* (5)) and every churn cap scaled by `years` then runs on a negative span. Under V06 §2.11's meaning, `years` is the first epoch's span.
required_change: §4.11 *The clock* (1): replace 'Its creation week is the present week of the dossier it is created from; a standalone map starts at week 0.' with 'Its present at creation is the dossier's present week (a standalone map's, week 0). Its **creation week** — the week of its `generate` event, its first model's — is that present, except on a history-first document, whose `generate` event stands at the replay's start, `W_p − round(52 × start.yearsAgo)` (V06 §3.20.3); the first epoch's `prevWeek` and `years` (above) read the creation week, and a replayed past lies between it and the present.' In EP-15 (l.8801), 'before a week-0 creation' reads 'before a week-0 present'. V06's end is VAT2-r2-04 (R2-05).

claim: Two crisis places have no reference line at a town no road reaches. §10.2 Crisis looks (d) defines the main approach road as 'the arterial out of the gate of greatest trade weight …, else the way of greatest trade weight leaving the built edge' (base l.15373–15375) and builds two places on it: approachByGate, the refugee camp ('the campLand faces along the main approach road by its gate, nearest V06's frontierFor', l.15381–15382), and outside, the quarantine camp ('the campLand faces furthest from the main approach road', l.15383). S3 (9) (a)'s mesa 'has no road in at generation and says so' (l.5381–5391), so no way leaves its built edge. Only approachRoads has a fallback there ('a place no road reaches (S3 (9) (a)'s unserved mesa) takes the campLand nearest its boundary'); V01 §3.18 defines campLand with no approach road and V07 §5.6 (7) the village rungs ('no entry — every camp on the campLand nearest the perimeter'), but at TOWN and above the refugee and quarantine camps have no line to rank by, and V06's frontierFor has no answer either (its no-frontier case is 'the approach road by a gate', R2-37 (6)). EP-27 names this mesa only for a siege; T-ER-27 has no such fixture.
required_change: §10.2 (d): 'With no main approach road (no way leaves the built edge — S3 (9) (a)'s unserved mesa), approachByGate takes the campLand faces nearest frontierFor's answer, else nearest the boundary point closest to the centre, and outside the campLand faces furthest from that point'. V06 §3.22 (2) (V06's end): frontierFor's no-frontier answer is then that boundary point. EP-27 and T-ER-27 add the unserved mesa with a refugee camp and a quarantine standing: each on campLand, else on the ring marks, never undefined.

claim: A siege's places read 'the outermost (standing) enceinte' — beyondWalls (base l.15376), outside (l.15383), edge (l.15388) and 'a siege of a place with no standing enceinte draws the blockade row' (l.15408) — undefined or wrong wherever a place's enceintes are not one nested series. Enceinte.kind includes bailey (§2.7 l.2236; Castle.curtain), so an unwalled town with a castle has a standing enceinte: its siege draws the trench and earthwork line 'round the walled arcs at the standoff', about 300 m round the castle, across the town's own plots and buildings, against the owner's 'an unwalled place gets blockade camps on its approach roads' (item 122 (b)). Rings that are not nested have no one outermost ring: a castle outside the town wall, a twin town's two rings (F-SITE's 'walls apart by the floor', l.8965), an aroundStage ring (§2.7 l.2242). And the siege line is kept off 'water, a way's carriageway, a gate's passage or a label's keep-out' only ((d), l.15370–15371), so it is drawn across extramural ribbon plots and buildings within the standoff of an ordinary walled town.
required_change: §10.2 (d): 'The walls a siege reads are the place's enceintes of kinds other than bailey (a castle's curtain only along its shared stretch with the town wall, Castle.cityWeld; its keep is gatesAndKeep's); outermost is the outer envelope of their walled arcs — for rings that are not nested, the walled arcs of each ring that no other ring encloses'; 'a place with no standing enceinte' reads 'no standing town enceinte', so an unwalled town with a castle draws the blockade on its approach roads; and the siege line and every camp are never drawn on a building footprint (burned farmsteads draw on their own), the line broken where it would cross an extramural plot's building. EP-27 and T-ER-27 add: an unwalled TOWN with an inside castle, a walled CITY with an outside castle, a twin town with two rings, and a walled town with extramural ribbons inside the standoff — 0 look pixels on a building footprint and the blockade at the castle-only town.

Owner rule 122 (b) maps mass immigration from 'regional_migration_pressure, REFUGEE_WAVE' to the refugee camp, and gives 'no look' only to the other regional_* pressures. claim: §4.4 S5a step 1 (l. 5715–5719) ends the stage-k ≥ 2 rule with 'a stage with no approachable arc takes §4.2 S3 (9)'s *every arc closed* — walled on the closing arcs whose row carries a wall, with one gate there, or walling nothing and recording no enceinte where no closing row carries one — and the arcs a land barrier closes are impassable to routes as the wall is (§4.2 S3 (7), (9))'. claim: §10.2 *Crisis looks* (f) (l. 15412) ends the disaster look as a whole: '`disaster`: (d)'s `neighbourhoods`, ending in the week its `reconstruction` Works begins (V06: no week draws both)'. claim: Inputs dangle before their milestones. §10.2's crisis looks land at M3b (l. 15345–15346; R2-36). Their placement reads V01's `disasterDistricts` for `neighbourhoods` and for `affectedQuarter`'s target matching (l. 15385, 15393), which V01 builds in W10 at M5 (V01 l. 3418), and V06's `frontierFor` for `approachByGate` (l. 15381–15382), which V06 builds in E2 at M6-E (V06 l. 4112). R2-36's 'a look or view whose subject is not yet built draws nothing of that part' is written in no design text.

required_change: §10.2's `CrisisLookRow`: add `label: string; icon?: string /* the display cells (V11 §2.3, V11 §3.1's *Display cells*): the words V09's Show crises list, Find's list of looks and §8.2's legend give the look; read by no stage */`.

claim: §10.2 *Crisis looks* is ambiguous about how a look's camped ground divides among its camps. (c) (l. 15363–15365) sizes by headcount with 'each army its own camp of `areaPerHeadM2` × its heads', but (d)'s `approachRoads` (l. 15379–15380) places 'one camp per road'. With the dossier's forces given, a one-army blockade of a town with four approach roads is one camp by (c) and four by (d). required_change: §10.2 *Crisis looks* (d), `approachRoads`: read '— the verges of each arterial leaving the settlement beyond its built edge, one camp per road, the look's camped ground divided equally among them (the remainder to the roads in trade-weight order); with the dossier's forces, each army's camp (c) whole on one road, the armies in descending size onto the roads in trade-weight order, a road taking a second army only when every road holds one; …'.

claim: §10.2 *Crisis looks*, the placement home, does not carry V07 §5.6's village readings, so V07's part has no implementer at its base end. These are V07's repair HAND-OFFS, not closed at their destination (principle (10)). (c) states no count for 'the share of its place's units': at small n (three outlying farms, a handful of palisade runs) a positive share can round to nothing while the look 'stands' — an undefined edge at every rung. V07 §5.6 (1) applies V01 §3.16 (5)'s round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] at the village rungs only. (d) defines the main approach road by §4.3's `TradeFlow` (a town's) and `affectedQuarter` as 'the district …'; a village holds one district, so `affectedQuarter` is the whole village. V07 §5.6 (2) reads them as the DR3-weighted `through` entry and one end; only `neighbourhoods` cites V07. (f) draws `siege`'s 'line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs' at every rung with walled arcs, and §8.2's siege row draws it. But item 122 (c) gives 'a hamlet … a war band's camp, a city a full siege line', and V07 §5.6 (1) and T-V7-69 (a) require no line at THORP or HAMLET. No V11 `scale` cell can suppress the line (they are camped-ground areas).
required_change: §10.2 *Crisis looks*: (c) after 'else the share of its place's units ((d))' add 'a share s of a place's n units takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s > 0 and none where s ≤ 0 — V01 §3.16 (5)'s count, one rule for every place at every rung'. (d) after 'Each place ranks its land or units, ties by the keyed draw:' add 'at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the main approach road, the outskirts' land and each place below read on the village's records as V07 §5.6 (2) states, `affectedQuarter` a unit of V07 §5.6 (3)'. (f) `siege`: 'a line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs at it' → 'at VILLAGE and above, a line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs at it — none at THORP and HAMLET, item 122 (c)'s war band's camp (V07 §5.6 (1))'. (h): 'THORP to the METROPOLIS cap: each rung's `scale` cell' → '…, and no siege line at THORP and HAMLET'.
